correctness.rationale: Complete proof derives unique positive attracting logistic pulse orbit and exact effort-to-closure-duration bijection for 0<A<4; the log-yield derivative has exactly one zero because L_A(s) strictly decreases and 1-exp(-s) strictly increases. The derivative of maximum in A is negative by an explicit scalar positivity inequality; conservation on a nonconstant logistic flight gives Y<rK/4. Series coefficients and exact derivative algebra were independently recomputed symbolically, and exact-rational exponential intervals verify a numerical case. Finite certificates are supplemental, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 13 October 2011 preprint arXiv:1110.6413v1, Section 6, expressly leaves the maximizing-effort problem for sustainable production unresolved while its Section 5 specializes to exactly the linear closed-season feedback treated here. Exact formulas, a unique global maximum, strict optimal-yield comparative static and quadratic small-feedback deficit were not found in the inspected fixed-period, general impulsive, or other periodic-closure sources. This is best-knowledge originality based on scientific implication comparisons, not a claim of exhaustive historical priority.
residual_risks: Exhaustive priority cannot be guaranteed; a later article citing the 2011 model might independently solve the same exact linear policy.
Bohner–Streipert 2016 was assessed from its abstract/model statement, not fully examined proof details.
Carvalho et al. 2019 manuscript download was inaccessible; abstract and method summary support a different policy but do not prove absence of a special-case equivalent result.
A general uninspected nonautonomous impulsive-harvest theorem could potentially imply parts of the continuous-harvest ceiling or optimization.

value.rationale: The motivating fishery article explicitly flags maximizing sustainable yield per unit time under catch-dependent closures as open. A complete unique optimizer and feedback-slope sensitivity for its explicit linear-policy benchmark are substantively relevant and are not a fixed-period substitute; the sharp small-feedback yield gap quantifies the cost of an actual management rule. The contribution is a natural exact classification, not an arbitrary parameter point, a numerical tolerance, or a routine restatement of general bounds.
